text:
Leevi Merilainen arrived in Vancouver on a waiver claim from Ottawa in late September, and he has ended up as the Canucks' workhorse: 14 games, 13 starts, a 2-8-1 record. The losses aren't all on him, but his numbers aren't hiding him either.

He has allowed 43 goals on 40.9 expected, 2.1 more than the shots usually produce. The split tells the story. On low-danger shots he has been sharp (.975 against a league .962). On the high-danger ones he has stopped .642 against .685, and his rebound rate (13.4% of saves lead to another shot within three seconds, league 10.7%) means too many plays get a second chance. His last five starts are 3.45 goals below expected.

Last season was harder still: 17.9 goals below expected in 20 games for Ottawa. Evolving-Hockey, on its own scale, liked his small 2024-25 sample and has been kinder this season than our numbers. Our talent range puts him just below a league-average stopper. What Vancouver needs is for the high-danger saves to catch up with the easy ones.
headline: Leevi Merilainen is carrying Vancouver's net, and it shows
